note: Real measured p95 budgets over the committed qualifying evidence (tools/client-perf/results/baseline.json, recorded on the physical mainstream-desktop device in qualification.devices). Every row is ceil(1.2 x merged p95) of the recorded repetitions: the p95 is computed over the concatenated repetitions of the cell's asset modes (the harness percentile semantics), and the fixed 20% margin is the documented allowance over the recorded physical repetitions, not a placeholder factor. The cells measure the real challenge configurations: Argon2id at the real adaptive-risk ladder target-4 rung (m=16384 KiB, t=3, p=1), the rsw time-lock rungs at T=75,000 / 150,000 / 300,000 squarings (the default rung, the midpoint and the protocol ceiling of 10,000..=300,000), SHA-256 at 16/18/20 bits, and the six ExecutionChallengeV1 cells (the files-tier execvm/execsha18/execargon/execchain and the inline-tier execvminline/execsha18inline), every execution cell measured at the manifest execution-version maximum (protocol/execution-v1.json max_execution_version, read at run time, never assumed). The interactive/non-interactive split is harness-owned: the client-perf.mjs difficulty profiles declare it (execchain carries interactive: false, models the composed chained-escalation flow, and is measured and budgeted like every cell but never counted as an ordinary interactive release cell and never ceiling-checked or engineering-target-checked); the budgets file declares no classification. The structured fields are authoritative. The absoluteP95Ceilings hard wall (5000 ms for mainstream-desktop) stays the hard failure for measured p95 in both validator modes and binds every interactive budget row; engineeringTargetP95 (4250 ms for mainstream-desktop: 85% of the wall) is the normal engineering ceiling an interactive release budget row may carry, hard in release certification and advisory in CI mode, so an interactive release budget can no longer sit at 94-95% of the human-facing wall. Routine challenges should target well below the engineering target, never near it. Budgets are derived from the committed evidence using the documented percentile and margin rules; structured budget fields are authoritative. absoluteP95Ceilings defines the hard interactive UX wall and engineeringTargetP95 defines the tighter release-certification target. Interactive classification is defined by the client-performance harness. Release certification requires current physical evidence for every tier in qualification.release_tiers; emulated and lab evidence are calibration evidence only. The qualified tier scope is mainstream-desktop only: it is the tier that represents the actual lab hardware, and the Android/iPhone emulation tiers (low-android, mid-android, flagship-android, older-iphone, current-iphone) and low-desktop carry no budget rows because emulation tiers are calibration signals, never release boundaries. qualification.release_tiers names the release-certification ladder (mainstream-desktop today); extending the ladder means adding that tier's p95 budget rows, its absoluteP95Ceilings entry, its engineeringTargetP95 entry and its physical-device evidence, never an invented tier name. The release-gate procedure is documented in tools/client-perf/README.md; extending the ladder follows the documented evidence procedure. History (re-records, retunes, prior audit rounds) belongs in the changelog, not in this file.
